claims.text: The material family is Al-containing multiphase AlxCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys with 1 < x < 2.
These alloys will exhibit a ductile-to-brittle-to-ductile transition during aging.
The non-monotonic ductility transition is driven by competition between loss of B2 chemical order and precipitation of secondary disordered phases.
Solutionized AlxCoCrFeNi in the stated composition range contains disordered FCC and ordered B2 phases.
The initial alloy has significant short-range and local chemical order around Al atoms.
Isothermal aging between 400°C and 600°C induces phase separation and order-disorder transitions in these alloys.
The targeted aging regime is below the B2 ordering temperature but above the phase-separation onset near 600°C or within the phase-separation regime.
During aging, the B2 phase composition shifts from Ni/Co/Al-rich to Fe/Cr-rich.
Aging changes both the B2 phase fraction and its long-range order.
A secondary disordered Fe/Cr-rich phase forms during aging.
Ordered B2 provides high strength but limited ductility.
Aging causes partial disordering or segregation of B2, including loss of Ni, Co, and Al.
Loss of B2 order or Ni/Co/Al reduces lattice friction and increases stacking-fault energy.
The proposed changes in lattice friction and stacking-fault energy enhance dislocation cross-slip and twinning.
Enhanced cross-slip and twinning restore ductility.
Ductility initially decreases as ordered B2 stabilizes or coarsens.
Ductility subsequently increases as B2 loses long-range order or decomposes into a disordered matrix.
The B2 ordering onset temperature increases from 1220°C at x = 1 to 1850°C at x = 2.
The phase-separation temperature is near 600°C.
The non-monotonic effect occurs only where ordered and disordered phases coexist and evolve independently.

contradictions.description: The intervention is restricted to 400–600°C, while the conditions call for temperatures above a phase-separation onset stated to be approximately 600°C. Most or all of the specified intervention range therefore cannot be above that onset.
The named ductile-brittle-ductile sequence requires a ductile initial state, but the mechanism describes the initial ordered-B2-dominated state as brittle.

Aging is specified far below the claimed B2 ordering temperatures, yet it is also proposed to cause a B2 order-disorder transition. No thermodynamic or compositional explanation reconciles disordering below the stated ordering boundary.
